definition: Subversion means the weakening or overthrowing of a system from within, by quiet, indirect means.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word subversion. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know subversion should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The commission found the exam board guilty of its own subversion: for years its appeals panel had quietly overturned every failing mark that carried the right family names.
Obstruction is milder than subversion: the institution's work is stalled and delayed, but its rules still mean what they say and its authority stands untouched.
Overthrow goes further than subversion: the institution is openly brought down, while subversion may leave every office and ordinance in place, working for someone else.

Sabotage wrecks a thing's operations with deliberate physical damage — stripped gears, salted fuel, a severed line — and it announces itself in wreckage. Subversion touches no equipment: it turns a system's own rules, offices, and trust against it, until the structure stands but no longer means anything.

A mutiny is open revolt — a crew or garrison refusing its own commanders to their faces, where everyone can see it. Subversion never announces itself: the subverter keeps every rule in plain view while quietly re-aiming what the rules do.

The checkers still met every Thursday; the checklist still hung by the door.
